titles.en: Who is the only true God?

zh-Hant: 今天的主題是：誰是獨一真神？
我們將會讀聖經，並且提出每個人都可能提出的終極問題：夠景誰是獨一真神？
為了找到答案，我們必須面對挑戰。
我們必須放下個人的意見、教派的聲明，甚至教會的傳統。或者你同我一樣，許多人從細個就被灌輸了各種關於神的言論。
在馬太福音15章6節,耶穌對這種危險提出了警告：「這就是你們藉著遺傳，廢了神的誡命。」對信仰最大的威脅，並非單純是錯誤的教導，而是把人為的傳統當成神的發言。
因此，為了真正理解聖經對獨一真神的啟示，我們必須讓神的話語直接觸動我們的心。神的真理是能清楚地揭示真神是誰。
讓我們跟隨耶穌，聆聽他在約翰福音17章3節的禱告。
“認識你─獨一的真神，並且認識你所差來的耶穌基督，這就是永生。”
耶穌的話語無比精確。
耶穌使用了確切的字詞：獨一的真神。
誰是獨一的真神？
他是指自己嗎？不是。
他說的是「你」
你是獨一的真神。
代名詞「你」的意思非常明確。
耶穌在向誰禱告？
耶穌在向父禱告，他在禱告中六次稱呼神為父。約翰福音17章1、5、11、21、24、25節。
父啊，你是獨一的真神。
對於誰是獨一的真神，這裡沒有任何模糊的地方。
耶穌在這裡談到「認識」。我們應當認識父，他是獨一的真神。我們從小在教會裡就被灌輸耶穌是神。但這與耶穌的話相違背。
讓我們放慢速度，仔細看看這節經文。
耶穌並沒有自稱為神。那麼，他在這裡是如何自稱的呢？
他自稱為基督。
基督並非指神。
基督是希臘文，是「彌賽亞」的意思，指的是神所膏立並差遣的那一位。
當我們跟隨耶穌時，必須認真對待他的話。在這段禱告中，耶穌告訴我們兩個關於永生的基本真理：
第一，要擁有永生，我們必須認識父，他是獨一真神。
第二，我們必須認識耶穌，他是父所差遣的彌賽亞。
新约的中心并不是问：耶稣是不是神?
這個問題從未在聖經中出現。
我们需要问的是: “耶稣是那位弥赛亚吗?”
這是每個門徒都必須回答的問題。
在這裡，耶穌在禱告中直接定義了神：父是「獨一真神」。
今天，我們將探討這四個字：獨一真神
要理解這些詞，我們需要查看希臘原文，也就是新約聖經的原文。
「獨一真神」這句話是 τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεόν. (ton monon alēthinon theon)
這四個希臘文都蘊含著精確的神學意義。它們共同構成了耶穌對神的定義。
讓我們仔細考察希臘文這四個字：
首先：τὸν (ton)
• τὸν 是希臘文中陽性單數定冠詞
• 這個定冠詞指向一個特定的、可辨識的位格
• 耶穌並非在談論“某一位神”或“泛指的神”
• 他指的是「那位神」－父。
神的這個身分指向一位特定的位格－父自己。
第二個希臘文：μόνον (monon)
• 希臘文 μόνον 源自字根 monos。
• Monos 的意思是獨一無二、單獨、專屬、「除此之外別無其他」。
• 在新約聖經中，μόνοs 總是表示獨特、絕對獨特。
• 根據定義，它排除所有其他事物。
請看看兩張圖片：
哪一張代表獨一無二？
左圖中，一頂王冠孤零零地矗(速)立著──獨一無二、独特、無與倫比、沒有對手。沒有其他。這就是 monos 的意思——獨一無二。
相較之下，右圖顯示的是幾個王冠中的一個。
這不是 monos。
這是幾個王冠中的一個。
這頂王冠並非獨一無二。
因為有其他王冠的存在，並且有相同的身份或類別。
左圖代表「獨一無二」。
而右圖則代表「幾個王冠中的一個」。
這種視覺化的概念有助於我們理解耶穌話語的精妙之處。
當耶穌稱父為「獨一真神」時，他是在宣告：
• 父是「獨一真神」。
• 沒有其他神能與他共享同一身分。
• 他不是任何群體中的一員。他不是兩個神或三個神其中的一個，也不是幾個神中的一個。
獨一真神意味著只有父是神。
第三個希臘字：ἀληθινὸν (alēthinon)
• Alethinon 的意思是：真的、真正的、真實的.
在希臘文中，Alethinon 用於對比：
• 真與假
• 真正的與偽造的
• 真實的與象徵性的
• 正統的與模仿的
所以，當耶穌稱父為「獨一真神」時，他是在說：父是獨一真真正正的神。他是真的、真正的、真實的。
第四個希臘文：θεόν (theon)
• θεόν 是 θεός 的受格形式。 θεός 的意思是「神」。
• 在希臘文新約聖經中，當 θεός 與定冠詞  ὁ θεός (ho theos) 連用時，它總是指聖父，而非耶穌。
• 這是一個重要的觀察。我們必須明確這個定義，否則我們可能會誤認為 θεός 指的是耶穌。
• 在整部新約聖經中，父是「ὁ θεός－神」。
綜上所述：耶穌對一神論的定義極為精準。
只有父是獨一真神。
Monotheism’ 的中文是 ‘一神论’
Mono 系 one,  一
Theism  系 God, 神
唯有父是 那唯独一的真神
我們可以用以下圖表來表示耶穌所定義的聖經一神論：
只有一位神:  一神論。
這位獨一真神就是父。
沒有其他任何一位與父同位。
神是「唯一、獨一的」。
讓我們來看看耶穌在另一處經文中也使用了同樣的希臘文短語：獨一的神。
約翰福音 5章44節
你們互相受榮耀，卻不求從獨一之神（τὸν　μόνον θεόν）來的榮耀，怎能信我呢？
這是耶穌的話。
希臘文片語「τὸν μόνον θεόν」（獨一的神）與約翰福音 17章3節 所使用的文法結構完全相同。
在這節經文中，「獨一的神」顯然指的是父神。
你可以從上下文看出這一點。
• 在第43節，耶穌明確提到了父－我奉我父的名來。
• 在第45節，耶穌再次提到了父。
因此，在第44節，當耶穌說「獨一的神」時，他顯然指的是父。
一切真正的榮耀都源自於獨一的真神，耶穌口中的父。
耶穌對比了兩種榮耀：
• 人的榮耀－我們彼此互相恭維
• 神的榮耀－來自獨一真神的榮耀。
耶穌他尋求的是來自神的榮耀，而不是來自人的榮耀，他也勸勉我們要這樣做。
這也是我的動力：尋求唯獨來自神的榮耀，而不是討人喜歡。我們很容易落入渴望得到　人認可和讚美　的陷阱。讓我們學習只為得到父神的認可而活。
既然我們已經了解了耶穌如何定義一神論，接下來讓我們看看他的門徒和使徒是如何肯定這真理的。
保羅在哥林多前書 8章6節 中說：“只有一位神，就是父。”
“獨一的神是父。”
唯獨父是獨一的神。
在羅馬書16章27節，保羅寫道：“願榮耀因耶穌基督歸與獨一全智的神，直到永遠。阿們。”
保羅使用了同樣的一神論詞彙——monos和theos——獨一的神。
一切榮耀都歸於獨一的神－藉著耶穌－而不是歸於耶穌。
在提摩太前書1章17節，保羅宣告：“但願尊貴、榮耀歸與那不能朽壞、不能看見、永世的君王、獨一的神，直到永永遠遠。阿們！。”
這裡再次使用了同樣的希臘文根：monos和theos。
耶穌並非這頌讚的接受者。
所有描述  ── 永世的君王、不能朽壞、不能看見、獨一的神 ── 都適用於天父。
在猶大書1章24-25節，耶穌的弟弟寫道：
“那能保守你們不失腳、叫你們無瑕無疵、歡歡喜喜站在他榮耀之前的我們的救主─ 獨一的神，  願榮耀、威嚴、能力、權柄，因我們的主耶穌基督歸與他，從萬古以前並現今，直到永永遠遠。阿們。”
猶大書使用了希臘文短語 “monos and theos”，意為“獨一的神”。他將「救主」的稱號指向獨一的神，而非耶穌。
耶穌並非頌讚的對象。相反，一切榮耀都藉著我們的主耶穌基督歸於獨一的神。
由此可見，新約作者的立場與耶穌親自教導的一神論完全一致。
這就引出了一個至關重要的問題：
既然耶穌和使徒們始終如一地教導，獨一的神是父，那麼如今主流教會的教導為何有所不同？
基督教自稱是一神論信仰，然而　對神的定義卻改變了。神不再被定義為“一”，而是“三位一體”。
「三位」被加在了「一」之上。
為什麼要加上「三位」呢？
加上「三位」之後，父就不再是獨一被稱為神的了。
「三位一體」直接與聖經關於「獨一的神」的明確教導相矛盾。
我們在整本聖經中都能看到「獨一真神」的說法。
但我們完全看不到「三位一體」的說法。
這應該提醒我們，耶穌最初教導的一神論教義中，已經添加了一個“新的”定義。
這「三位」指的是什麼？
這「三位」代表三位格，每一位都被稱為神。
聖父是神。
聖子是神。
聖靈是神。
如果每個位格都是完全的神，並且三位都是同等、永恆，那麼必然是有三位神。
神變成了一個群体，一個由三位組成的群体，因此有了「三位一體」的說法，即三位一體。
當「三位」與「一」結合時，神就不再是「獨一無二」的了。
你明白现在在发生了什么事吗?
加上「三位一體」從根本上改變了神的身份。它背離了耶穌親自給的定義:　一位神，就是父。
教會給的新定義是：三位一體的神，聖父、聖子、聖靈。
令人震驚的是：
大多數基督徒沒有意識到，「神」一詞的定義在教會歷史中已經改變了。
如今的教會不再堅持耶穌親自給予的神定義。
三位一體的概念並非源自耶穌的教導，也並非源自使徒的教導。
三位一體的概念源自於公元4世紀所製定的教會會議和信經, 距离耶稣在地上已经三百年了。
今天，許多基督徒對此仍然一無所知：
三位一體的神定義並非源自新約聖經的教導，而是來自後來的教會傳統。我曾經也是對此一無所知的基督徒之一。我從小就認為教會的信經就是耶穌的教導。
大多數基督徒從未仔細研究教會的信經，看看它們是否反映了耶穌的教導。相反，他們像我一樣，只是簡單地遵循代代相傳的傳統，卻沒有意識到神的定義在幾個世紀以來已經發生了變化。
這對我們是至關重要。
因為一旦對神的定義偏離了耶穌的教導，我們對永生的理解就不再建立在他的真理之上。
永生取決於認識獨一真神以及他所差來的彌賽亞耶穌。我們不能將信仰建立在另一個神定義之上, 一個耶穌從未給予的定義。
因此，擺在我們面前的問題非同小可：
教會是如何偏離耶穌在聖經中所給神的定義？
教會是如何從耶穌清晰定義的　父是獨一真神　轉變，將神描述為三位一體的？
這種根本性的轉變需要我們認真而誠實地審視，以便我們能夠分辨我們的信仰是建立在耶穌對神的定義之上，還是建立在後來的教會傳統之上。
若我們重新定義神時，我們也重新定義了我們整個信仰的根基。
我們將在接下來的課堂中共同探討這些重要的真理。
Shalom. 我祈禱我們能歸回到耶穌所啟示的神 -- 獨一真神，雅偉，父。下星期見。
01 Who is the only true God?
Shalom, I’m Rosa.
Today’s topic is: Who is the only true God?
We’re going to look into Scripture and ask the ultimate question any human can ask: Who is the only true God?
To find the answer, we must do something challenging.
We must set aside human opinions, denominational statements, and even church traditions passed down to us. Like me, many of us grew up with a lot of noise about what people had told us about God.

Jesus warns about this danger in Mt 15:6: You make void the word of God for the sake of your tradition. The greatest threat to faith is not always false teaching, but too many human traditions claiming to speak for God.
So, to truly understand what the Bible reveals about the one true God, we must let the Word of God speak directly to our hearts. God’s truth always brings perfect clarity about who the true God is.
Let’s follow Jesus and listen to his prayer in John 17:3
“This is eternal life: that they know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.”
Jesus’ words are incredibly precise.
Jesus uses the exact words: the only true God.
Who is the only true God?
Does he point to himself as the only true God? No.
He says “You” – You are the only true God.
The pronoun “You” is not vague.
Who is Jesus praying to?
Jesus is praying to the Father, whom he addresses 6 times in his prayer.  John 17:1, 5, 11, 21, 24,25.
You Father, You are the only true God.
There is no ambiguity as to who the only true God is.
Jesus speaks about “knowing” here. We are to know the Father as the only true God.  But we have been brought up in our churches to believe Jesus is God. This contradicts Jesus’ words.
Let’s slow down and look at this verse carefully.
Jesus does not identify himself as God. How does he identify himself here?
He identifies himself as Christ.
Christ does not mean God.
Christ is the Greek word for Messiah, the one anointed and sent by God.
When we follow Jesus, we must take his words seriously. And in his prayer here, Jesus tells us two essential truths about eternal life:
First, to have eternal life, we must know the Father as the only true God
Second, we must know Jesus as the Messiah sent by the Father.
The central question in the NT is not: “Is Jesus God?
This question never appears in the Bible.
The real question is:  Is Jesus the Messiah?
This is the question every disciple must answer.
Here, Jesus gives us a direct definition of God in his prayer: the Father is “the only true God”
Today, we will explore these 4 words: The Only True God
To understand these words, we need to look at the Greek words, the original language of the New Testament.
The phrase  “the only true God” is τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεόν. (ton monon alēthinon theon)
Each of these four Greek words carries precise theological meaning. Together, they form Jesus' own definition of God.
Let’s examine these four words carefully:
First:  τὸν (ton) is “The”
Ton is the singular masculine definite article in Greek
The article points to a specific, identifiable person
Jesus is not speaking about “a god” or “god in general”
He is speaking about “the God”– the Father.
This identity of God points to one specific Person – the Father Himself.
The second Greek word: μόνον (monon)
The Greek word μόνον comes from the root monos.
Monos means one and only, alone, exclusive, “no other besides”.
In the New Testament usage, μόνοs always means one and only, absolutely unique.
It excludes all others by definition.
Take a look at the following two images:
Which one represents the one and only?
In the left image, the single crown stands alone – unique, unmatched, without rivals. There is no other. This is the meaning of monos – the one and only.
By contrast, the image on the right shows a crown among many crowns.
This is not monos.
This is one of many.
The crown is not unique.
Other crowns also exist and share the same identity or category.
The left image represents “the one and only”.
Whereas the right image represents “one of many”.
This visual concept helps us grasp the precision of Jesus’ words.
When Jesus calls the Father “the only true God’, he is declaring:
the Father is “the one and only God”.
There is no other who shares His identity.
He is not one member of a group. Not one of two. Not one of three, not one of many.
(Back to the slide of the Greek the only true God)
The one and only God means that the Father alone is the God.
The third Greek word: ἀληθινὸν (alēthinon)
Alethinon means: true, genuine, real, authentic
In Greek, ἀληθινός is used to contrast:
true vs. false
genuine vs counterfeit
real vs symbolic
authentic vs imitation
So when Jesus calls the Father “the only true God”, he is saying: The Father is the only God who is truly God. He is genuine, real, and authentic.
The fourth Greek word:  θεόν (theon)
θεόν is the accusative form of θεός. Θεός means “God”.
In the Greek New Testament, when θεός appears with the definite article (ὁ θεός), it consistently refers to the Father, never to Jesus.
This is an important observation. We must be clear about this definition, or else we may mistakenly think θεός refers to Jesus.
Throughout the New Testament, the Father is “ὁ θεός - the God”.
Putting This All Together: Jesus defines Monotheism with absolute precision.
“Mono” means “one” and “Theism” means God.
The Father alone is the one and only true God.
We can put Biblical monotheism, as defined by Jesus, into the following diagram format:
There is One God – monotheism.
The One God is the Father.
No one else shares that identity.
God is “the one and only”.
Let’s look at another Bible verse from Jesus where he uses the same Greek phrase: the only God
John 5:44  How can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the (τὸν) only (μόνον) God (θεόν) ?
These are Jesus’ words.
The Greek phrase “Ton monon theon (τὸν μόνον θεόν) the only God” is the exact same grammatical construction used in John 17:3.
In this verse, “The only God” clearly refers to the Father.
You can see this from the immediate context.
In verse 43, Jesus explicitly mentions the Father – I have come in my Father’s name.
In verse 45, Jesus speaks of the Father again.
So in verse 44, when Jesus says “the only God”, he is clearly referring to the Father.
All true glory originates from the one God, the Father.
Jesus is contrasting  two kinds of glory:
human glory – we give praises to one another
divine glory – the glory that comes from the only God.
Jesus himself seeks the glory that comes from God, not from humans, and he urges us to do the same.

This is also my motivation, to seek the glory that comes from God alone, and not be a men-pleaser. It is so easy to fall into the trap of craving human approval and human praise. Let us learn to live for the Father’s approval alone.
Now that we have seen how Jesus defines monotheism, let’s look at how his disciples and apostles affirm the exact same truth.
Paul says in 1 Cor 8:6  There is one God, the Father.
The one God is the Father.
The Father alone is the one God.
In Rom 16:27, Paul writes, “ to the only wise God be glory forevermore through Jesus Christ! Amen.
Paul uses the same monotheistic vocabulary – monos and theos – the only God.
All glory goes to the only God  –  through Jesus – not to Jesus.
In 1 Timothy1:17, Paul declares:  To the King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
Again, the same Greek root words are used: monos and theos.
Jesus is not the recipient of this doxology.
Every description --  the King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God -- applies to the Father.
In Jude 1:25, Jesus’ own brother writes:
“To the only God, our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority, before all time and now and forever. Amen.
Jude uses the Greek phrase – monos and theos - the only God.  He applies the title “Savior” to the only God, not to Jesus.
Jesus is not the recipient of the doxology. Rather, all glory flows through Jesus Christ, our Lord, to the only God.
As you can see, the  New Testament writers stand in perfect harmony with the monotheism Jesus himself teaches.
This then raises a crucial question for us.
Since Jesus and the apostles consistently teach that the one God is the Father, why does the mainstream Church teach something different today?
Christianity claims to be a monotheistic faith, yet the definition of God has changed.  God is no longer defined as one, but as three-in-one.
The “three” has been added to the “one”.
Why add the three?
By adding the three, the Father is no longer the only One called God.
Adding the number three directly contradicts the Bible's explicit teaching about the “one God”.
We see the “one God” throughout the Bible.
We don’t see the phrase “three-in-one” at all.
This should alert us that a “new” definition has been added to the original teaching of monotheism that Jesus taught.
What is the three?
The three represent three persons, each of whom is called God.
The Father is God.
The Son is God.
The Holy Spirit is God.
If each person is fully God and all three are coequal and coeternal, then it is unavoidable that there are three Gods.
God has become a group, one group of three, thus the term “three-in-one’, three in a group.
When “three” is added to “one”, God is no longer “the one and only.”
Can you see what happened?
Adding the three fundamentally changes the identity of God. It moves away from the definition Jesus himself gives – one God, the Father.
The new definition the Church gave: three-in-one God, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
And here is the shocking part:
Most Christians do not realize  that the definition of the word “God” has changed over time in Church history.
The Church today no longer holds to the definition of God Jesus himself gives.
The three-in-one does not come from Jesus’ teaching at all. It does not come from the apostles.
The three-in-one comes from Church councils and Church creeds developed in the 4th Century – long after Jesus walked on this earth.
And this is where many Christians are left in the dark:

The three-in-one definition of God does not come from the New Testament teaching, but from later Church tradition. I was one of those Christians who never knew this. I grew up assuming that the Church creeds were simply Jesus’ teaching.

Most Christians never examine the Church creeds to see whether they reflect Jesus’ own teaching. Instead, like me, they simply follow the traditions handed down to them, without realizing the definition of God has changed over the centuries.
Over time, the word “God” expanded to include three persons – a conclusion that is contrary to the biblical texts.
And this matters deeply to us.
Because once the definition of God shifts away from what Jesus taught, our understanding of eternal life  is no longer grounded in his truth.
Eternal life depends on knowing the only true God and Jesus the Messiah whom He sent. We cannot afford to build our faith on a different definition of God that Jesus never gave.
So the question before us is not a small one:
How did the Church drift away from the Biblical definition of God Jesus gave?
How did the Church move from Jesus’ clear definition of one God – the Father – to describing God as  three-in-one?
This radical shift demands careful and honest examination, so that we can discern whether our faith is built on Jesus’ definition of God or on a later church tradition.
The moment we redefine God, we redefine the foundation of our entire faith.
We will explore these important truths together in the upcoming sessions.
Shalom, this is Rosa.  My prayer is that we would return to the God Jesus revealed – the only true God, Yahweh, the Father. See you next week.
